SMART CURRENCY GROUP LIMITED
GROUP STRATEGIC REPORT
FOR THE 52-WEEK PERIOD FROM 30 SEPTEMBER 2024 TO 28 SEPTEMBER 2025
Introduction
The Directors present their strategic report for Smart Currency Group Limited for the 52 week period from 30 September 2024 to 28 September 2025.
Business review
The principal activity of the Company is the provision of foreign currency spot/forward/option contracts on a non-advisory basis for private individuals and corporate clients. The Companies operations are based in the UK and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority ("FCA").
The Group's revenue increased by 34.7% to £28,922,694 (2024: £21,472,519). Strengthening the Group's balance sheet continues to be a key area of focus, with shareholder funds increased at period end by 9.2% to £19,181,516 (2024: £17,560,103).
Growth in revenue is due to the improvement in Smart Currency Options Limited ("Options"), a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, where last year we de-risked our concentration risk by bringing on new clients and increasing our Option client base by >50%. This put us in a much stronger position in the current financial year, having a larger client base. Smart Currency Exchange Limited ("Exchange"), a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company that services Spot/Forward products saw some modest growth year on year as the Private Client division began to recover from previously communicated headwinds.
We continue to remain debt free and maintain a strong focus on our cash position across the Group, with increasing unrestricted cash being our primary goal. With the increase in interest rate environment, this has benefited us due to our cash position and we have generated the equivalent of 7.89% of our income figure through interest.
The Directors are satisfied with the performance of the Group. Our main goals for the year ahead are to, increase revenue from our larger client base, on-board more clients, continue to improve our cash position, automate processes to enable us to scale more effectively and continue to provide a high value service so that we retain 100% of our clients.
Page 1

GROUP STRATEGIC REPORT (CONTINUED)

Principal risks and uncertainties
The key risks facing the Group and the Company are as follows:
Liquidity Risk Management: The risk that the Group may not have sufficient liquid resources to meet its obligations. The Group manages Liquidity by ensuring that it has enough liquidity to meet its margin requirements under both normal and stressed conditions. Client margin requirements fund the majority of the Company's own margin requirements, which is why there are strict processes enforced. But having a strong cash flow and unrestricted cash balance allows the Group to meet its own margin requirements under stressed conditions even in scenarios where clients would be delayed on meeting their margin requirements with the Group.
Credit Risk Management: Failure of a client to settle a contracted trade exposes us to a loss equal to the fair value of the trade. This credit risk arises when a client's total funds deposited with the Group are insufficient to cover the trading losses incurred. To minimise this risk, the Group has detailed credit procedures and ongoing monitoring to keep client exposures to acceptable levels. The Group does this predominantly by limiting the amount of credit given to a client, ensuring that their financials support the level of credit, as well as strictly enforcing margin call policies. The Group stress tests the positions of every client on a regular basis, making clients aware of their risk profile for margin calls and regularly review client's updated financials.
Operational Risk: The Group maintains policies and procedures to control and mitigate risk in all areas of operations. The senior management team monitors operational risks on a daily basis with key information reported to Directors and Senior Management. The Group also covers risk through insurance and considers its cover in all material areas of risk.
Conflicts: Global events such as the war in Ukraine and in Gaza have had significant impacts on world trade, energy costs, interest rates, and the cost of living which have and continue to impact businesses and individuals. These risks are constantly assessed by senior management as to their impact on the Group's business and its clients.
A quarterly risk committee is held with the board and key senior management personnel where all risks are updated on.
Key performance indicators
The key KPI's for the Group are revenue growth, pre-tax profits growth, net margin percentage (pre-tax profits/revenue) and total equity.

Long Term Decisions
The interests and views of our shareholders, the directors and other stakeholders are all considered when making long term decision. Consideration of the Group's vision, mission and ultimate objective are part of this process, thereby ensuring the decisions are of optimum long-term benefit to all our stakeholders.
Employee engagement
The Group's success has been built on the quality, loyalty and dedication of our people. We develop our employees and encourage them to progress internally. Our key values that each employee strives to deliver are Customer Service, Owning Their Own Development, Growth Mindset, Taking Responsibility, Working as a Team and Owning the Conversation.
Supplier and Customer engagement
The business has forged long term relationships with it's banking partners, which has enabled close working relationships that is critical to our business longevity and success.
Client retention is one of our KPI's that is monitored weekly, we provide a high value service to our customers to differentiate ourselves from competitors.
Impact of the Group's operations on the community and the environment
The Group's impact on the local community is positive, providing employment and supporting local charities, the main one being Solidarity Sports, who harness the transformative power of play to nurture disadvantaged children recovering from complex trauma. As a Group, we are constantly looking for ways to reduce our carbon footprint.
Reputation for a high standard of business conduct
The Group has a robust system of governance and risk management in place to ensure a high standard of business conduct. These include governance processes around decision making on people, information security, privacy, and operational risks.
The need to act fairly as between members of the Group
The Group is privately owned by the directors who all have critical roles in the day to day running of the business. As such there is no issue of inequitable treatment between the members.
Future Developments
The Group continues to invest in the core business as it looks to increase income and improve profitability. Key areas of investment are in personnel, technology and infrastructure.
Regulations and authorisation
Smart Currency Exchange Limited is a payments services company trading in foreign exchange spot and forward contracts offering client hedging solutions. It is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority under the payment services Regulation 2009 (FRN 504509) for the provision of payment fees and is regulated by HMRC as a money transmitter (MLR 12198457).
Smart Currency Options Limited is a company whose principal activity is the provision of foreign currency options on a non-advisory basis for corporate clients. It is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FRN 656427).

1. General information
Smart Currency Group Limited (the 'Company') is a private limited company (limited by shares)
incorporated in England and Wales (registration number 08029548).
The principal activity of the parent is that of a holding company and that of subsidiaries are: foreign
currency trading, option trading, consultancy, and holding company.
The address of the registered office is 9th Floor, 1 Lyric Square, Hammersmith, London, United Kingdom,
W6 0NB.
2. Accounting policies
2.1 Basis of preparation of financial statements
The financial statements have been prepared under the historical cost convention unless otherwise
specified within these accounting policies and in accordance with Financial Reporting Standard 102,
the Financial Reporting Standard applicable in the UK and the Republic of Ireland and the
Companies Act 2006.
The preparation of financial statements in compliance with FRS 102 requires the use of certain
critical accounting estimates. It also requires Group management to exercise judgement in applying
the Group's accounting policies (see note 3).
The Company has taken advantage of the exemption allowed under section 408 of the Companies
Act 2006 and has not presented its own Statement of comprehensive income in these financial
statements.
The following principal accounting policies have been applied:
2.2 Basis of consolidation
The consolidated financial statements present the results of the Company and its own subsidiaries
("the Group") as if they form a single entity. Intercompany transactions and balances between group
companies are therefore eliminated in full.
The consolidated financial statements incorporate the results of business combinations using the
purchase method. In the Statement of financial position, the acquiree's identifiable assets, liabilities
and contingent liabilities are initially recognised at their fair values at the acquisition date. The results
of acquired operations are included in the Consolidated statement of comprehensive income from the
date on which control is obtained. They are deconsolidated from the date control ceases.
2.3 Going concern
The directors recognise that the current global economic disruptions through the Ukraine-Russia war,
interest rate rises and cost of living crisis are likely to put pressure on the private client division's
growth in the short term as has been highlighted in the current financial year business review. The
directors have set a formal budget for 2025/26, which take into consideration these potential risks in
the forthcoming year. The forecast for the business for the 12 months from the date of signing these
financial statements demonstrates that the Group will continue to be profitable and grow its balance
sheet and cash balances over this period. Performance against budget is reviewed monthly. The
directors believe that the continued investment in people, processes and technology will facilitate
continued improvement in growth of the business.
Following this assessment the directors have a reasonable expectation that the Group has adequate
resources to continue in operational existence for the foreseeable future. Accordingly, the directors
continue to apply the going concern basis in preparing the consolidated financial statements.

2. Accounting policies (continued)
2.4 Revenue
The Company is an investment holding company.
The Group's revenue is generated from three subsidiaries:
Smart Currency Exchange Limited — revenue of this company is the difference between the cost and the selling price of a currency to clients and is recognised at the point of sale. Point of sale is the contractual agreement to sell one currency and purchase another between this company and the clients for either immediate or forward delivery. When this company enters into a contract with a client, it also enters into a matched contract with its banks. This means the revenue is certain at the point of sale.
The Overseas Guides Company Limited — revenue is measured at fair value of the consideration received or receivable, excluding discounts, rebates, value added tax and other sales taxes. The following criteria must also be met before turnover is recognised: This company's single source of revenue is derived from supply of support services and introduction of their readers to specialist partners. Revenue from shows is recognised when invoice is raised, revenue from subscription/advertising is recognised in the month the subscription/advertising relates to and revenue from commission is recognised once the introduction is complete. All the revenue streams is recognised to the extent that it is probable that the economic benefits will flow to the Company and the turnover can be reliably measured.
Smart Currency Options Limited — revenue is recognised to the extent that it is probable that the economic benefits will flow to the Company and the turnover can be reliably measured. Revenue is measured as the fair value of the consideration received or receivable, excluding discounts, rebates, value added tax and other sales taxes. Revenue of the Company, being the difference between the value of the selling price of an option contract to the client and its underlying purchase cost to the Company, is recognised at the point of sale.

2.6 Tangible fixed assets
Tangible fixed assets under the cost model are stated at historical cost less accumulated
depreciation and any accumulated impairment losses. Historical cost includes expenditure that is
directly attributable to bringing the asset to the location and condition necessary for it to be capable of
operating in the manner intended by management.
Depreciation is charged so as to allocate the cost of assets less their residual value over their
estimated useful lives, using the straight-line method.
Depreciation is provided on the following basis:
Fixtures and fittings | - | 25% per annum
Office equipment | - | 25% per annum
The assets' residual values, useful lives and depreciation methods are reviewed, and adjusted
prospectively if appropriate, or if there is an indication of a significant change since the last reporting
date.
Gains and losses on disposals are determined by comparing the proceeds with the carrying amount
and are recognised in the Consolidated statement of comprehensive income.
2.7 Investments
Investments in subsidiaries are measured at cost less accumulated impairment. Where merger relief
is applicable, the cost of the investment in a subsidiary undertaking is measured at the nominal value
of the shares issued together with the fair value of any additional consideration paid.
Unlisted investments are included at cost less impairments. Profits and losses arising from disposals
of fixed asset investments are treated as part of the result from ordinary activities.
2.8 Debtors
Short-term debtors are measured at transaction price, less any impairment. Loans receivable are
measured initially at fair value, net of transaction costs, and are measured subsequently at amortised
cost using the effective interest method, less any impairment.
2.9 Cash and cash equivalents
These comprise cash at bank and other short-term highly liquid bank deposits with an original
maturity of three months or less.
2.10 Financial instruments
Spot/Forward/Option foreign currency contracts are non-basic financial instruments. The Group
enters into an FX contract with its bank that mirrors the contract that the Client has booked with the
Group, therefore no risk is taken by the Group with respect to Client contracts. These contracts are
initially recognised at fair value on the date an FX contract is entered into and are subsequently re-
measured at their fair value.
In addition, the Group enters into forward foreign currency contracts within its own capacity to
mitigate margin requirements based on exchange rate risk across group companies. This scenario
arises where the net Delta position in one entity is opposite to another entity. Placing equal and
opposite forward contracts in these entities, allows the Group to reduce margin requirements and net
exposures. As the positions are equal and opposite, no market risk is taken by the Group. Changes
in the fair value of these forward contracts are recognised through Statement of Comprehensive
Income under the headings 'Realised (loss)/gain on forward contracts' and 'Unrealised (loss)/gain on

2.11 Creditors
Short-term creditors are measured at the transaction price. Other financial liabilities, including bank
loans, are measured initially at fair value, net of transaction costs, and are measured subsequently at
amortised cost using the effective interest method.
2.12 Foreign currency translation
Functional and presentation currency
The Company's functional and presentational currency is GBP.
Transactions and balances
Foreign currency transactions are translated into the functional currency using the spot exchange
rates at the dates of the transactions.
At each period end foreign currency monetary items are translated using the closing rate. Non-
monetary items measured at historical cost are translated using the exchange rate at the date of the
transaction and non-monetary items measured at fair value are measured using the exchange rate
when fair value was determined.
Foreign exchange gains and losses resulting from the settlement of transactions and from the
translation at period-end exchange rates of monetary assets and liabilities denominated in foreign
currencies are recognised in the Consolidated statement of comprehensive income except when
deferred in other comprehensive income as qualifying cash flow hedges.
All other foreign exchange gains and losses are presented in the Statement of Comprehensive
Income within 'Administrative expenses'.
2.13 Operating leases: the Group as lessee
Rentals paid under operating leases are charged to the Consolidated statement of comprehensive
income on a straight-line basis over the lease term.
Benefits received and receivable as an incentive to sign an operating lease are recognised on a
straight-line basis over the lease term, unless another systematic basis is representative of the time
pattern of the lessee's benefit from the use of the leased asset.

2.14 Pensions
Defined contribution pension plan
The Group operates a defined contribution plan for its employees. A defined contribution plan is a pension plan under which the Group pays fixed contributions into a separate entity. Once the contributions have been paid the Group has no further payment obligations.
The contributions are recognised as an expense in the Consolidated statement of comprehensive income when they fall due. Amounts not paid are shown in accruals as a liability in the Statement of financial position. The assets of the plan are held separately from the Group in independently administered funds.
2.15 Interest income
Interest income is recognised in the Consolidated statement of comprehensive income using the effective interest method.
2.16 Taxation
Tax is recognised in the Consolidated statement of comprehensive income except that a charge attributable to an item of income and expense recognised as other comprehensive income or to an item recognised directly in equity is also recognised in other comprehensive income or directly in equity respectively.
The current income tax charge is calculated on the basis of tax rates and laws that have been enacted or substantively enacted by the reporting date in the countries where the Company and the Group operate and generate income.
Deferred tax balances are recognised in respect of all timing differences that have originated but not reversed by the reporting date, except that:
• The recognition of deferred tax assets is limited to the extent that it is probable that they will be recovered against the reversal of deferred tax liabilities or other future taxable profits;
• Any deferred tax balances are reversed if and when all conditions for retaining associated tax allowances have been met; and
• Where they relate to timing differences in respect of interests in subsidiaries, associates, branches and joint ventures and the Group can control the reversal of the timing differences and such reversal is not considered probable in the foreseeable future.
Deferred tax is determined using tax rates and laws that have been enacted or substantively enacted by the reporting date.

2.17 Share-based payments
In the Group accounts, where share options are awarded to employees in group companies in
respect of the Company's shares, fair value of the options is determined at the date of grant and
charged to profit or loss over the vesting period. The credit entry is recorded in a capital contribution
reserve within equity. The fair value is based upon the Black-Scholes model which is a well-accepted
model for the valuation of share options where there are no market conditions attached. Non-market
vesting conditions are taken into account by adjusting the number of equity instruments expected to
vest at each Statement of Financial Position date so that, ultimately, the cumulative amount
recognised over the vesting period is based on the number of options that eventually vest.
The Company has no employees. In the Company accounts the share-based payment charge in
relation to awards made to employees of other group companies has been recognised as capital
contribution resulting in an increase in the investment in subsidiaries.
2.18 Dividends
Equity dividends are recognised when they become legally payable. Interim equity dividends are
recognised when paid. Final equity dividends are recognised when approved by the shareholders at
an annual general meeting.
